about: Does turning off Wi-Fi and Bluetooth save battery. Factory #37, backlog row 42, slug wifibattery. One hard idea: Apple says Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 'are designed to draw minimal power from the battery when they aren't connected' and tells you to keep them on; on iPhone the Control Center Wi-Fi button doesn't even turn Wi-Fi off (it disconnects, Wi-Fi stays available for AirDrop and Location, auto-join returns by 5 a.m.); Apple says Wi-Fi uses less battery than cellular; Google's one exception: turn off Bluetooth to stretch a dying battery. Check yours in Settings › Battery. Sources read 2026-11-20, see BRIEF.md.

lines.text: Apple says Wi-Fi and Bluetooth draw minimal power when not connected.

It just disconnects. Wi-Fi stays available for AirDrop.
And auto-join comes back by 5 in the morning.

lines.text: Apple even says Wi-Fi uses less battery than cellular.
Battery nearly dead? Google says turn Bluetooth off.
Check yours: Settings, Battery, not the toggles.
Still switching Wi-Fi off? Yes or no.
